commitResults.messageTitle: Complete increment Level-5. Modularised command handling and introduced better OOP compliance.
Add date validation for deadlines and events
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline and event commands accept arbitrary text for their date fields.

Malformed dates can be stored and displayed, leading to inconsistent
task data and unclear user input errors.

Require /by, /from, and /to values to use the dd-mm-yyyy format. Reject
dates that do not represent valid calendar dates.

Use strict parser-level validation so all chatbot commands enforce the
same date rules before tasks are created.

Deadline and event commands accept dates in DD-MM-YYYY format but do not
support optional times, and task displays expose the raw input format.

Users cannot record precise times or read dates in a concise, consistent
format.

Accept optional HH:MM times in 24-hour format for /by, /from, and /to.
Format valid dates and times as readable values (e.g. Oct 15 2019,
6:00pm). Store event start and end values in separate persistence
fields.

commitResults.messageTitle: Store dates as Java time values
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline and event tasks store their date and time values as strings.

String storage does not model calendar dates or optional times reliably.

Store deadline and event dates as LocalDate fields and optional times as
LocalTime fields. Parse and format these values through DateTimeParser.

Echo mixes command execution with scanner input and response formatting.

This makes Echo responsible for presentation details and makes the
application harder to test independently.

Extract console interaction into new Ui class and expose immutable task
snapshots.

A dedicated Ui separates user interaction from command parsing and task
operations while preserving the existing command flow.

TaskList stores tasks in memory and persists them into a file.

This mixes collection management with file system access and spreads
persistence behaviour across TaskList and TaskManager.

Extract file loading, saving, and task deserialisation into Storage.
Ensure TaskList manages only in-memory tasks, and make TaskManager
persist each successful mutation.

Centralising persistence gives file operations one clear owner while
preserving the existing file format and task behaviour.

Echo delegates startup construction to TaskManager, which loads saved
tasks and creates Storage implicitly.

This hides application dependencies and prevents Echo from handling
loading failures directly.

Move storage creation and task loading into Echo. Add file-path and
dependency-injection constructors, catch loading failures, and pass the
loaded TaskList and Storage to TaskManager.

Make Echo the composition root so TaskManager focuses on task operations
while startup behaviour remains explicit and testable.

Echo dispatches parsed commands through a switch statement.

This couples the application loop to every command's behaviour and
requires Echo to change whenever commands are added.

Make Command an abstract executable base class. Move the existing
dispatch logic into ParsedCommand, and have CommandParser return
executable commands.

This gives future command classes a common execute and isExit contract
while preserving the current parser and task behaviour during migration.

ParsedCommand handles bye by displaying farewells and reporting session
exit.

This keeps exit-specific behaviour inside the temporary compatibility
comand and requires ParsedCommand to retain a special case for session
lifecycle control.

Extract bye handling into ExitCommand and make CommandParser return it
for bye.

ParsedCommand handles help and list through its shared command switch.

This keeps display behaviour coupled to the temporary compatibility
command and requires that class to know about every command type.

Extract HelpCommand and ListCommand, and make CommandParser create these
dedicated commad objects.

Each display command now owns its own UI behaviour while sharing the
common Command execution contract.

PasedCommand handles mark, unmark, and delete through its shared command
switch.

This couples task-number behaviour to the temporary compatibility
command and duplicates the responsibility of interpreting task numbers.

Extract TaskNumberCommand as a shared base class, then add MarkCommand,
UnmarkCommand, and DeleteCommand.

The shared base class centralises one-based task-number handling while
each subclass owns its specific task operation and UI response.

ParsedCommand handles todo, deadline, and event creation through its
shared comand switch.

This couples task construction and display behaviour to the temporary
compatibility command.

Extract TaskCreationCommand as a shared base clss, then add TodoCommand,
DeadlineCommand, and EventCommand.

The shared base class centralises description handling and creation
responses while each subclass owns its specific TaskManager operation.

CommandParser still relies on the temporary ParsedCommand compatibility
class.

This leaves obsolete indirection in the command hierarchy after all
supported commands have dedicated implementations.

Remove ParsedCommand and make CommandParser return the appropriate
concrete command class for every supported command.

This completes the polymorphic command design and lets Echo interact
with all commands through the common execute and isExit contract.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor: organise classes into cohesive packages
commitResults.messageBody:
All Java classes currently reside in the default package.

The project needs a scalable package structure as the number of classses
grow.

Group related classes into echo.command, echo.task, echo.storage,
echo.ui, and echo.util packages.

Keep src/main/java as the source root while separating responsibilities
into cohesive packages.
